    25→export function setupSmokeSuite(suiteName: string): () => SmokeTestRuntime {

    47→      "authenticate with SurrealDB",

    51→    await withTimeout(() => surreal.use({ namespace }), 10_000, "switch to test namespace");
    52→    await withTimeout(() => surreal.query(`DEFINE DATABASE ${database};`), 10_000, "define test database");
    53→    await withTimeout(
    54→      () => surreal.use({ namespace, database }),

    58→
    59→    const schemaSql = readFileSync(join(process.cwd(), "schema", "surreal-schema.surql"), "utf8");
    60→    await withTimeout(() => surreal.query(schemaSql), 20_000, "apply schema");
    61→
    62→    // Reserve a port so betterAuth gets the real URL at init time
    63→    const tempServer = Bun.serve({ port: 0, fetch: () => new Response() });
    64→    const reservedPort = tempServer.port;
    65→    tempServer.stop(true);
    66→    const baseUrl = `http://127.0.0.1:${reservedPort}`;
    67→
    68→    const config: ServerConfig = {

   100→      chatAgentModel: deps.chatAgentModel,

   177→    throw new Error(`Failed to create test user (${response.status}): ${body}`);
   178→  }
   179→
   180→  const setCookie = response.headers.getSetCookie();
   181→  if (!setCookie || setCookie.length === 0) {
   182→    throw new Error("Sign-up did not return session cookies");
   183→  }
   184→
   185→  const cookieHeader = setCookie.map((c) => c.split(";")[0]).join("; ");
   186→  return { headers: { Cookie: cookieHeader } };
   187→}
   188→
   189→export async function collectSseEvents<T extends { type: string }>(streamUrl: string, timeoutMs: number): Promise<T[]> {
   190→  const response = await fetch(streamUrl, { headers: { Accept: "text/event-stream" } });
   191→  if (!response.ok || !response.body) {
   192→    throw new Error(`Failed to open SSE stream (${response.status})`);
   193→  }
   194→
   195→  const reader = response.body.getReader();
   196→  const decoder = new TextDecoder();
   197→  const events: T[] = [];
   198→  let buffer = "";
   199→
   200→  const timeout = setTimeout(() => {
   201→    void reader.cancel();
   202→  }, timeoutMs);
   203→
   204→  try {
   205→    while (true) {
   206→      const { value, done } = await reader.read();
   207→      if (done) {
   208→        break;
   209→      }
   210→
   211→      buffer += decoder.decode(value, { stream: true });
   212→      const segments = buffer.split("\n\n");
   213→      buffer = segments.pop() ?? "";
   214→
   215→      for (const segment of segments) {
   216→        const dataLine = segment.split("\n").find((line) => line.startsWith("data: "));
   217→        if (!dataLine) {
   218→          continue;
   219→        }
   220→
   221→        const event = JSON.parse(dataLine.slice("data: ".length)) as T;
   222→        events.push(event);
   223→
   224→        if (event.type === "error") {
   225→          const errorText = (event as { error?: string }).error;
   226→          throw new Error(`SSE error event: ${errorText ?? "unknown error"}`);
   227→        }
   228→
   229→        if (event.type === "done") {
   230→          return events;
   231→        }
   232→      }
   233→    }
   234→  } finally {
   235→    clearTimeout(timeout);
   236→    reader.releaseLock();
   237→  }
   238→
   239→  return events;
   240→}
   241→
   242→export async function fetchJson<T>(url: string, init?: RequestInit): Promise<T> {
   243→  const response = await fetch(url, init);
   244→  if (!response.ok) {
   245→    const body = await response.text();
   246→    throw new Error(`Request failed (${response.status}) ${url}: ${body}`);
   247→  }
   248→
   249→  return (await response.json()) as T;
   250→}
   251→
   252→function base64url(buf: Buffer): string {
   253→  return buf.toString("base64url");
   254→}
   255→
   256→function generatePkce(): { verifier: string; challenge: string } {
   257→  const verifier = base64url(randomBytes(32));
   258→  const challenge = base64url(createHash("sha256").update(verifier).digest());
   259→  return { verifier, challenge };
   260→}
   261→
   262→/**
   263→ * Obtain an OAuth2 JWT access token for MCP endpoints.
   264→ * Requires a SurrealDB connection to skip consent screen.
   265→ */
   266→export async function getOAuthToken(
   267→  baseUrl: string,
   268→  surreal: Surreal,
   269→  sessionHeaders: Record<string, string>,
   270→  scopes: string = "graph:read graph:reason session:write offline_access",
   271→): Promise<string> {
   272→  // Trigger JWKS key generation if not yet done
   273→  await fetch(`${baseUrl}/api/auth/jwks`);
   274→
   275→  const dcrRes = await fetch(`${baseUrl}/api/auth/oauth2/register`, {
   276→    method: "POST",
   277→    headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
   278→    body: JSON.stringify({
   279→      client_name: `smoke-test-${Date.now()}`,
   280→      redirect_uris: ["http://127.0.0.1:9999/callback"],
   281→      grant_types: ["authorization_code", "refresh_token"],
   282→      response_types: ["code"],
   283→      token_endpoint_auth_method: "none",
   284→    }),
   285→  });
   286→  if (!dcrRes.ok) throw new Error(`DCR failed: ${dcrRes.status} ${await dcrRes.text()}`);
   287→
   288→  const { client_id } = (await dcrRes.json()) as { client_id: string };
   289→
   290→  await surreal.query(`UPDATE oauthClient SET skipConsent = true WHERE clientId = $cid;`, {
   291→    cid: client_id,
   292→  });
   293→
   294→  const { verifier, challenge } = generatePkce();
   295→  const authUrl = new URL(`${baseUrl}/api/auth/oauth2/authorize`);
   296→  authUrl.searchParams.set("client_id", client_id);
   297→  authUrl.searchParams.set("redirect_uri", "http://127.0.0.1:9999/callback");
   298→  authUrl.searchParams.set("response_type", "code");
   299→  authUrl.searchParams.set("scope", scopes);
   300→  authUrl.searchParams.set("state", "test-state");
   301→  authUrl.searchParams.set("code_challenge", challenge);
   302→  authUrl.searchParams.set("code_challenge_method", "S256");
   303→  authUrl.searchParams.set("resource", baseUrl);
   304→
   305→  const authRes = await fetch(authUrl.toString(), {
   306→    headers: sessionHeaders,
   307→    redirect: "manual",
   308→  });
   309→  if (authRes.status !== 302) throw new Error(`Authorize did not redirect: ${authRes.status}`);
   310→
   311→  const location = authRes.headers.get("location")!;
   312→  const redirectUrl = new URL(location, baseUrl);
   313→  const code = redirectUrl.searchParams.get("code") ?? "";
   314→  if (!code) throw new Error(`No code in redirect: ${location}`);
   315→
   316→  const tokenRes = await fetch(`${baseUrl}/api/auth/oauth2/token`, {
   317→    method: "POST",
   318→    headers: { "Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" },
   319→    body: new URLSearchParams({
   320→      grant_type: "authorization_code",
   321→      code,
   322→      redirect_uri: "http://127.0.0.1:9999/callback",
   323→      client_id,
   324→      code_verifier: verifier,
   325→      resource: baseUrl,
   326→    }),
   327→  });
   328→  if (!tokenRes.ok) throw new Error(`Token exchange failed: ${tokenRes.status} ${await tokenRes.text()}`);
   329→
   330→  const tokens = (await tokenRes.json()) as { access_token: string };
   331→  return tokens.access_token;
   332→}
   333→
   334→export type TestUserWithMcp = TestUser & {
   335→  mcpHeaders: Record<string, string>;
   336→};

   338→/**
   339→ * Create a test user with both session cookie and OAuth MCP token.
   340→ */
   341→export async function createTestUserWithMcp(
   342→  baseUrl: string,
   343→  surreal: Surreal,
   344→  suffix: string,
   345→  scopes?: string,
   346→): Promise<TestUserWithMcp> {
   347→  const user = await createTestUser(baseUrl, suffix);
   348→  const accessToken = await getOAuthToken(baseUrl, surreal, user.headers, scopes);
   349→  return {
   350→    ...user,
   351→    mcpHeaders: { Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}` },
   352→  };
   353→}
   354→
   355→function requireTestEnv(name: string): string {
   356→  const value = process.env[name];
   357→  if (!value || value.trim().length === 0) {
   358→    throw new Error(`Smoke test requires env var ${name}`);
   359→  }
   360→  return value;
   361→}

   363→async function withTimeout<T>(callback: () => Promise<T>, timeoutMs: number, label: string): Promise<T> {
   364→  return await Promise.race([
   365→    callback(),
   366→    new Promise<T>((_, reject) => {
   367→      setTimeout(() => reject(new Error(`Timed out: ${label}`)), timeoutMs);
   368→    }),
   369→  ]);
   370→}

     1→import { verifyAccessToken } from "better-auth/oauth2";
     2→
     3→export type BrainTokenClaims = {
     4→  sub: string;
     5→  scope?: string;
     6→  aud?: string;
     7→  iss?: string;
     8→  exp?: number;
     9→  iat?: number;
    10→  "urn:brain:workspace"?: string;
    11→  "urn:brain:workspace_name"?: string;
    12→  "urn:brain:agent_type"?: string;
    13→  [key: string]: unknown;
    14→};
    15→
    16→/**
    17→ * Create a JWT validator that verifies access tokens using the auth server's JWKS.
    18→ * Tokens must be JWTs (issued when `resource` param is passed during authorization).
    19→ */
    20→export function createJwtValidator(issuerUrl: string) {
    21→  // issuerUrl is the server baseURL (e.g. "http://localhost:3000").
    22→  // Better Auth mounts at /api/auth (basePath), so JWKS and issuer include that path.
    23→  const authBase = issuerUrl.endsWith("/api/auth") ? issuerUrl : `${issuerUrl}/api/auth`;
    24→  const jwksUrl = `${authBase}/jwks`;
    25→  const issuer = authBase;
    26→
    27→  return async (token: string): Promise<BrainTokenClaims> => {
    28→    const payload = await verifyAccessToken(token, {
    29→      jwksUrl,
    30→      verifyOptions: {
    31→        issuer,
    32→        audience: issuerUrl,
    33→      },
    34→    });
    35→    return payload as BrainTokenClaims;
    36→  };
    37→}
    38→

import "../env/index.mjs";
import { APIError } from "better-call";
import { betterFetch } from "@better-fetch/fetch";
import { UnsecuredJWT, createLocalJWKSet, decodeProtectedHeader, jwtVerify } from "jose";

//#region src/oauth2/verify.ts
/** Last fetched jwks used locally in getJwks @internal */
let jwks;
/**
* Performs local verification of an access token for your APIs.
*
* Can also be configured for remote verification.
*/
async function verifyJwsAccessToken(token, opts) {
	try {
		const jwt = await jwtVerify(token, createLocalJWKSet(await getJwks(token, opts)), opts.verifyOptions);
		if (jwt.payload.azp) jwt.payload.client_id = jwt.payload.azp;
		return jwt.payload;
	} catch (error) {
		if (error instanceof Error) throw error;
		throw new Error(error);
	}
}
async function getJwks(token, opts) {
	let jwtHeaders;
	try {
		jwtHeaders = decodeProtectedHeader(token);
	} catch (error) {
		if (error instanceof Error) throw error;
		throw new Error(error);
	}
	if (!jwtHeaders.kid) throw new Error("Missing jwt kid");
	if (!jwks || !jwks.keys.find((jwk) => jwk.kid === jwtHeaders.kid)) {
		jwks = typeof opts.jwksFetch === "string" ? await betterFetch(opts.jwksFetch, { headers: { Accept: "application/json" } }).then(async (res) => {
			if (res.error) throw new Error(`Jwks failed: ${res.error.message ?? res.error.statusText}`);
			return res.data;
		}) : await opts.jwksFetch();
		if (!jwks) throw new Error("No jwks found");
	}
	return jwks;
}
/**
* Performs local verification of an access token for your API.
*
* Can also be configured for remote verification.
*/
async function verifyAccessToken(token, opts) {
	let payload;
	if (opts.jwksUrl && !opts?.remoteVerify?.force) try {
		payload = await verifyJwsAccessToken(token, {
			jwksFetch: opts.jwksUrl,
			verifyOptions: opts.verifyOptions
		});
	} catch (error) {
		if (error instanceof Error) if (error.name === "TypeError" || error.name === "JWSInvalid") {} else if (error.name === "JWTExpired") throw new APIError("UNAUTHORIZED", { message: "token expired" });
		else if (error.name === "JWTInvalid") throw new APIError("UNAUTHORIZED", { message: "token invalid" });
		else throw error;
		else throw new Error(error);
	}
	if (opts?.remoteVerify) {
		const { data: introspect, error: introspectError } = await betterFetch(opts.remoteVerify.introspectUrl, {

Found it. Look at line:

```js
let jwks;
```

This is a **module-level singleton**. The `getJwks` function caches the JWKS globally:

```js
if (!jwks || !jwks.keys.find((jwk) => jwk.kid === jwtHeaders.kid)) {
    jwks = ... // fetch from jwksUrl
}
```

With `--concurrent`, multiple smoke test files run in the same process. Each creates its own better-auth server with **different JWKS keys** (different DB namespaces). But `verifyAccessToken` uses a **single global `jwks` cache**. 

The first test suite to verify a token fetches and caches its JWKS. When the oauth-mcp-auth test tries to verify its tokens, the cached JWKS has different keys → signature verification fails silently → falls through to `if (!payload)` → throws "no token payload" → caught as 401.

The fix: run the oauth-mcp-auth test in isolation, or ensure it runs first before other tests cache different JWKS. But the proper fix is to not use `--concurrent` for smoke tests, or to work around the cache.

Confirmed. Multiple smoke test files use OAuth tokens: `intent-context.test.ts`, `commit-check-endpoint.test.ts`, `session-no-status-change.test.ts`, plus `oauth-mcp-auth.test.ts`. With `--concurrent`, they all run in the same process and share the global `jwks` cache in `@better-auth/core/dist/oauth2/verify.mjs`.

The race: whichever test file fetches JWKS first poisons the cache for all others (different DB = different keys but same `kid` lookup falls through incorrectly, or different `kid` triggers a re-fetch from the wrong URL).

The fix is to bypass the global cache by creating our own validator that always fetches fresh JWKS. Let me update `token-validation.ts`.

  "old_string": "import { verifyAccessToken } from \"better-auth/oauth2\";\n\nexport type BrainTokenClaims = {\n  sub: string;\n  scope?: string;\n  aud?: string;\n  iss?: string;\n  exp?: number;\n  iat?: number;\n  \"urn:brain:workspace\"?: string;\n  \"urn:brain:workspace_name\"?: string;\n  \"urn:brain:agent_type\"?: string;\n  [key: string]: unknown;\n};\n\n/**\n * Create a JWT validator that verifies access tokens using the auth server's JWKS.\n * Tokens must be JWTs (issued when `resource` param is passed during authorization).\n */\nexport function createJwtValidator(issuerUrl: string) {\n  // issuerUrl is the server baseURL (e.g. \"http://localhost:3000\").\n  // Better Auth mounts at /api/auth (basePath), so JWKS and issuer include that path.\n  const authBase = issuerUrl.endsWith(\"/api/auth\") ? issuerUrl : `${issuerUrl}/api/auth`;\n  const jwksUrl = `${authBase}/jwks`;\n  const issuer = authBase;\n\n  return async (token: string): Promise<BrainTokenClaims> => {\n    const payload = await verifyAccessToken(token, {\n      jwksUrl,\n      verifyOptions: {\n        issuer,\n        audience: issuerUrl,\n      },\n    });\n    return payload as BrainTokenClaims;\n  };\n}",
  "new_string": "import { createRemoteJWKSet, jwtVerify } from \"jose\";\n\nexport type BrainTokenClaims = {\n  sub: string;\n  scope?: string;\n  aud?: string;\n  iss?: string;\n  exp?: number;\n  iat?: number;\n  \"urn:brain:workspace\"?: string;\n  \"urn:brain:workspace_name\"?: string;\n  \"urn:brain:agent_type\"?: string;\n  [key: string]: unknown;\n};\n\n/**\n * Create a JWT validator that verifies access tokens using the auth server's JWKS.\n * Tokens must be JWTs (issued when `resource` param is passed during authorization).\n *\n * Uses jose's createRemoteJWKSet directly instead of better-auth's verifyAccessToken\n * because the latter uses a module-level JWKS singleton cache that breaks when\n * multiple test servers (each with their own JWKS keys) run concurrently.\n */\nexport function createJwtValidator(issuerUrl: string) {\n  // issuerUrl is the server baseURL (e.g. \"http://localhost:3000\").\n  // Better Auth mounts at /api/auth (basePath), so JWKS and issuer include that path.\n  const authBase = issuerUrl.endsWith(\"/api/auth\") ? issuerUrl : `${issuerUrl}/api/auth`;\n  const jwksUrl = new URL(`${authBase}/jwks`);\n  const issuer = authBase;\n\n  // createRemoteJWKSet maintains its own per-URL cache with proper key rotation\n  const getKey = createRemoteJWKSet(jwksUrl);\n\n  return async (token: string): Promise<BrainTokenClaims> => {\n    const { payload } = await jwtVerify(token, getKey, {\n      issuer,\n      audience: issuerUrl,\n    });\n    return payload as BrainTokenClaims;\n  };\n}"
}

> AGENT

Still 4 failures with `--concurrent`! Look at the output order:
```
(fail) MCP route with wrong workspace [3.52ms]     ← runs immediately
(pass) setup: create workspace [453.37ms]           ← finishes AFTER other tests
```

The issue isn't JWKS caching — it's that `--concurrent` runs ALL `it()` blocks concurrently within a file. The `it("setup: ...")` hasn't finished setting `fullToken` and `workspaceId` before other tests use them.

The fix: convert the setup `it()` to a `beforeAll` within the describe block.

> AGENT

All 4 OAuth tests now pass with `--concurrent`. The remaining failure is unrelated (US-UI-004 identity spoke test).

**Root cause**: `bun test --concurrent` runs all `it()` blocks concurrently within a file. The test used `it("setup: ...")` to set shared state (`fullToken`, `workspaceId`), but other tests started before setup finished.

**Fix**: Converted the setup `it()` to `beforeAll`, which bun guarantees completes before any test case runs. Also replaced `better-auth/oauth2`'s `verifyAccessToken` with direct `jose` `createRemoteJWKSet` to avoid a module-level JWKS singleton cache (a latent bug that would surface if different test servers had different `kid` values).

Let me check the workspace bootstrap to understand the timing, then fix the retry.

> AGENT

The bootstrap is `await`ed before the response returns. The issue is that with `--concurrent`, all 5 `it()` blocks run simultaneously — 5 concurrent sign-ups + 3 concurrent workspace creations hitting the same test server. The bootstrap silently fails under load (caught at line 185).

Fix: share a single user+workspace via `beforeAll` so the heavy setup happens once before concurrent assertions.

**Summary of fixes:**

1. **`tests/smoke/oauth-mcp-auth.test.ts`** — Converted `it("setup: ...")` to `beforeAll`. With `--concurrent`, bun runs all `it()` blocks in parallel, so the setup hadn't finished setting `fullToken`/`workspaceId` before other tests used them.

2. **`tests/smoke/unified-identity/auth-rewiring.test.ts`** — Same pattern: moved user+workspace creation into a shared `beforeAll`. Five concurrent `it()` blocks each creating users and workspaces overloaded the test server, causing silent identity bootstrap failures.

3. **`app/src/server/mcp/token-validation.ts`** — Replaced `better-auth/oauth2`'s `verifyAccessToken` with direct `jose` `createRemoteJWKSet` + `jwtVerify`. The better-auth function uses a module-level JWKS singleton cache that would break if concurrent test servers ever generated different key IDs.

     1→## Git Commits
     2→
     3→- Always use `--no-verify` when committing. The pre-commit hook requires `brain init` which is not available in worktree environments.
     4→
     5→## Data Value Contract
     6→
     7→- Never persist, publish, or return `null` for domain data values (Surreal records, API payloads, events, UI state).
     8→- Absence must be represented by omitted optional fields only (`field?: Type`), not by `null`.
     9→- If `null` appears in domain data, treat it as a contract violation and fix the producer. Do NOT sanitize/coerce it at consumers.
    10→
    11→## TypeScript Conventions
    12→
    13→- Do NOT use `null`. Use `undefined` via optional properties (`field?: Type`) instead.
    14→- Do NOT create wrapper/helper functions for simple operations. Cast directly with `as`.
    15→- Type result payloads once and avoid repetitive per-field casting.
    16→
    17→
    18→
    19→## LLM Tool Definitions (Vercel AI SDK)
    20→
    21→- Tool `description` is for *what the tool does* and *when to use it*. Keep it concise.
    22→- Parameter-level guidance belongs on `.describe()` in the Zod `inputSchema`, not in the tool description or system prompt.
    23→- For enums, put per-value guidance in `.describe()` on the enum field — the `ai` SDK converts Zod `.describe()` to JSON Schema `description` at every level.
    24→- Do NOT duplicate tool descriptions or parameter guidance in the system prompt. The LLM already receives tool definitions via the `tools` API parameter.
    25→- System prompt should only contain information the LLM cannot get from tool definitions: dynamic context, rendering format instructions, and cross-cutting architectural rules.
    26→
    27→## Extraction Schema (Structured Output)
    28→
    29→- Azure/OpenRouter structured output requires every property in `properties` to be listed in `required`. Zod `.optional()` fields are excluded from `required` in the generated JSON schema, causing provider rejection.
    30→- Do NOT use `.optional()` in `extractionResultSchema` or its nested entity schemas (`app/src/server/extraction/schema.ts`).
    31→- To represent absence, add a `"none"` sentinel to the enum and strip it to `undefined` via `.transform()` after parsing. The transform is applied during Zod validation but does not affect the JSON schema sent to the provider.
    32→- Existing pattern: `assignee_name` and `resolvedFromMessageId` use union variants (each variant has the field as required) instead of optional fields.
    33→
    34→## Schema & Data Migration
    35→
    36→- This project does NOT maintain backwards compatibility with existing data. Schema changes are breaking.
    37→- Do NOT write data migration or backfill scripts. Old data is discarded on schema changes.
    38→- New fields should be required (not optional) from the start — no need for `option<...>` to accommodate pre-existing records.
    39→
    40→### SurrealDB Schema Migration Workflow
    41→
    42→- Create a versioned `.surql` migration script for each schema change.
    43→- Migration filenames MUST use a zero-padded autoincrement numeric prefix, followed by an underscore and slug (for example `schema/migrations/0008_add_task_priority.surql`).
    44→- Determine the next prefix by scanning `schema/migrations` and incrementing the highest existing prefix. Do NOT reuse or renumber existing migration files.
    45→- Apply migrations with `bun migrate` — the migration runner (`schema/migrate.ts`) tracks applied migrations in a `_migration` table and only runs pending ones.
    46→- Do NOT apply migrations manually via `surreal import` or raw HTTP calls — always use `bun migrate`.
    47→- Wrap migration scripts in `BEGIN TRANSACTION; ... COMMIT TRANSACTION;` so they succeed or fail atomically.
    48→- `DEFINE ANALYZER` cannot run inside a transaction in SurrealDB v3.0. Place it before the `BEGIN TRANSACTION;` block.
    49→- Prefer `DEFINE ... OVERWRITE` or `ALTER TABLE` / `ALTER FIELD` for schema evolution; reserve `IF NOT EXISTS` for bootstrap-only creation.
    50→- SurrealDB does NOT support `ALTER TABLE ... ADD FIELD`. To add fields to existing tables, use `DEFINE FIELD OVERWRITE <field> ON <table> TYPE <type>;`.
    51→- When removing fields, update schema and stored rows in the same migration (`REMOVE FIELD ...; UPDATE ... UNSET ...;`).
    52→- Verify applied schema with `INFO FOR TABLE <table>;` in the target namespace/database.
    53→
    54→### SurrealDB Existing Data Migration (Explicit Exception Only)
    55→
    56→- Default project policy is still no backfills; only run existing-data migrations when explicitly requested by the user.
    57→- Snapshot before mutation with `surreal export --ns <namespace> --db <database> <backup-file>`.
    58→- Run data transforms in versioned `.surql` scripts applied via `bun migrate`.
    59→- Use a transaction for multi-step migrations:
    60→  - `BEGIN TRANSACTION;`
    61→  - apply schema updates (`DEFINE ... OVERWRITE` / `ALTER`)
    62→  - backfill with `UPDATE ... WHERE ...`
    63→  - rewrite relationships with `RELATE` (do NOT use `CREATE` for `TYPE RELATION` tables)
    64→  - clean old keys with `REMOVE FIELD ...; UPDATE ... UNSET ...;`
    65→  - `COMMIT TRANSACTION;`
    66→- In this codebase, represent missing values as omitted fields / `NONE` (never `null`) during data transforms.
    67→- Validate scripts with `surreal validate <migration-file>` before apply if the `surreal` CLI is available.
    68→- Verify result counts and shape after apply (`SELECT count() ...`, `INFO FOR TABLE ...`).
    69→
    70→## Fire-and-Forget & Inflight Tracking
    71→
    72→- Do NOT use `void` for fire-and-forget DB operations in route handlers. Background work that uses the SurrealDB connection will fail with `ConnectionUnavailableError` when smoke tests close the DB in `afterAll`.
    73→- Route-level async work (e.g. `processGitCommits`, `processChatMessage`) must be tracked via `deps.inflight.track(promise)`. The `InflightTracker` (`runtime/types.ts`) lets smoke tests `drain()` pending work before closing connections.
    74→- Nested async work inside tracked parents (e.g. `seedDescriptionEntry`, `fireDescriptionUpdates`, `persistEmbeddings`) should use `await ... .catch(() => undefined)` instead of `void`. Since the parent is already background work, awaiting doesn't affect user-facing latency.
    75→- When adding new background DB operations in route handlers, always use `deps.inflight.track()` or `await` within an already-tracked parent.
    76→
    77→## Failure Handling
    78→
    79→- Do NOT add fallback logic that masks invalid state, malformed payloads, or contract violations.
    80→- Fail fast: throw immediately when required data is missing or does not match the expected shape.
    81→- Prefer explicit hard failures over silent degradation, synthetic defaults, or "best effort" recovery.
    82→- Only introduce fallback behavior when explicitly requested, and document the reason in code comments.
    83→- Never silently ignore errors (e.g. empty `.catch(() => {})`). Always surface them via logging or re-throw.
    84→
    85→## Schema Awareness
    86→
    87→- Always read `schema/surreal-schema.surql` before writing queries, seed data, or any code that creates/updates SurrealDB records. The schema defines required fields, types, and relations — guessing leads to silent `SCHEMAFULL` rejections.
    88→
    89→## Testing Setup
    90→
    91→- Install deps: `bun install`
    92→- Run deterministic unit tests (no LLM/API calls): `bun test tests/unit/`
    93→- Run smoke test: `bun test tests/smoke/`
    94→- Run eval suite: `bun run eval`
    95→- Run eval watch mode: `bun run eval:watch`
    96→- Agents must not run evals directly. Delegate eval execution to the user and ask them to run eval commands and share results.
    97→
    98→### Smoke Test Isolation
    99→
   100→- Smoke tests create an isolated Surreal namespace/database, apply `schema/surreal-schema.surql`, run assertions, then remove the test DB/namespace.
   101→- Smoke tests require a reachable SurrealDB server at `SURREAL_URL` with credentials from env.
   102→- Smoke tests boot a dedicated app server process with test `SURREAL_NAMESPACE`, `SURREAL_DATABASE`, and `PORT`; do not point smoke runs at shared production-like DBs.
   103→
   104→### Eval Requirements
   105→
   106→- Evals call the real extraction model through existing app wiring.
   107→- Required env: `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and `EXTRACTION_MODEL` (set to Haiku model when needed).
   108→- Optional env:
   109→  - `AUTOEVAL_MODEL` for `autoevals` factuality scorer model override.
   110→  - `EVAL_RESULTS_DIR` for evalite sqlite output.
   111→  - `EVAL_CACHE_DIR` for extraction eval cache.
   112→
   113→### Evalite Silent Failure Mode
   114→
   115→- Evalite (v0.19+) silently swallows errors thrown in `beforeAll` hooks. When `beforeAll` fails, all evals show `Score: -`, `Duration: 0ms`, and no error output.
   116→- If evals show this pattern, the cause is almost always a thrown error during setup — typically a missing env var in `setupEvalRuntime` (which calls `requireEnv` for all model IDs).
   117→- To diagnose: check that all required env vars are set, or temporarily wrap `beforeAll` contents in try/catch with `console.error` to surface the real error.
   118→
   119→## Server Architecture Overview
   120→
   121→- Entrypoint is `app/server.ts`; it only calls `startServer()` from `app/src/server/runtime/start-server.ts`.
   122→- Runtime bootstrap is split into:
   123→  - `runtime/config.ts` (env parsing/validation)
   124→  - `runtime/dependencies.ts` (Surreal + model clients)
   125→  - `runtime/start-server.ts` (route registration + Bun server startup)
   126→- HTTP cross-cutting concerns live in `app/src/server/http`:
   127→  - `request-logging.ts` (request context + top-level error boundary)
   128→  - `response.ts` (JSON/headers helpers)
   129→  - `parsing.ts` (request/form-data parsing)
   130→  - `errors.ts` + `observability.ts` (error/log primitives)
   131→- SSE state management is isolated in `app/src/server/streaming/sse-registry.ts`.
   132→- Route/business domains are separated by workflow:
   133→  - `workspace/*` for workspace create/bootstrap/scope checks
   134→  - `chat/*` for ingress, chat agent, async message processing
   135→  - `entities/*` for entity search, detail, actions, and work item accept endpoints
   136→  - `onboarding/*` for onboarding state and guided replies
   137→  - `extraction/*` for extraction generation, persistence, dedupe/upsert, embeddings, and context loaders
   138→  - `agents/*` for specialized subagent implementations (PM agent)
   139→  - `observation/*` for observation CRUD queries
   140→- `graph/*` contains reusable Surreal graph queries used by chat/tools and higher-level workflows.
   141→
   142→### Chat Agent Architecture
   143→
   144→The chat system uses a thin orchestrator pattern where a single top-level chat agent dispatches to specialized subagents. The knowledge graph is the communication bus — agents read from and write to the graph independently, never passing data directly between each other.
   145→
   146→```
   147→User Message
   148→  │
   149→  ├─→ Extraction Pipeline (always runs, Haiku)
   150→  │     └─→ entities/relationships → SurrealDB graph
   151→  │
   152→  └─→ Chat Agent (Sonnet, thin orchestrator)
   153→        ├─→ Direct tools (search, entity detail, decisions, observations)
   154→        └─→ Subagent dispatch
   155→              └─→ PM Agent (Haiku) → suggestions, observations → graph
   156→```
   157→
   158→**Two paths to the graph:**
   159→| Source | Path | Why |
   160→|--------|------|-----|
   161→| User messages | Extraction pipeline (Haiku infers entities from unstructured text) | User input is unstructured |
   162→| Agent output | Direct graph write (agents already have structured form) | Nothing to extract |
   163→
   164→**Key files:**
   165→- `chat/handler.ts` — `runChatAgent()`: streams chat agent responses with tool use
   166→- `chat/context.ts` — `buildChatContext()` / `buildSystemPrompt()`: loads graph context, builds chat agent system prompt
   167→- `chat/tools/index.ts` — `createChatAgentTools()`: registers all chat agent tools
   168→- `chat/tools/types.ts` — `ChatToolExecutionContext`: actor-typed context (`chat_agent | mcp | pm_agent`)
   169→
   170→### Chat Agent Tools
   171→
   172→| Tool | Purpose |
   173→|------|---------|
   174→| `search_entities` | Search workspace entities by text query |
   175→| `get_entity_detail` | Fetch entity with relationships and provenance |
   176→| `get_project_status` | Project task/decision/question aggregation |
   177→| `get_conversation_history` | Load recent conversation messages |
   178→| `create_provisional_decision` | Draft a decision for user review |
   179→| `confirm_decision` | Finalize a decision (requires explicit user auth) |
   180→| `resolve_decision` | Mark a decision as resolved |
   181→| `check_constraints` | Validate decision constraints |
   182→| `create_observation` | Create observation for risks/conflicts/signals |
   183→| `acknowledge_observation` | Mark observation as reviewed |
   184→| `resolve_observation` | Close a resolved observation |
   185→| `invoke_pm_agent` | Delegate to PM subagent |
   186→
   187→### Shared Tool Layer
   188→
   189→Tools live in `chat/tools/` as composable building blocks. Any agent (chat agent, PM subagent, future subagents) can compose the tools it needs. Key shared tools for work item management:
   190→
   191→| Tool | File | Purpose |
   192→|------|------|---------|
   193→| `suggest_work_items` | `chat/tools/suggest-work-items.ts` | Batch triage/dedup (>0.97 exact duplicate, ≥0.8 merge, <0.8 new) |
   194→| `create_work_item` | `chat/tools/create-work-item.ts` | Direct entity creation in graph |
   195→
   196→### Product Manager Subagent
   197→
   198→The PM agent (`agents/pm/`) is the single authority on tasks, features, and project status. It uses the AI SDK's `ToolLoopAgent` class and composes shared tools from `chat/tools/`. It is invoked by the chat agent via `invoke_pm_agent` tool with an intent:
   199→
   200→| Intent | When to use |
   201→|--------|-------------|
   202→| `plan_work` | User discusses goals, features, or work to be done |
   203→| `check_status` | User asks about project status, progress, or blockers |
   204→| `organize` | User wants to restructure or re-prioritize |
   205→| `track_dependencies` | User asks about blocked items or dependency chains |
   206→
   207→**Key files:**
   208→- `agents/pm/agent.ts` — `runPmAgent()`: creates `ToolLoopAgent` with PM tools, returns structured JSON output
   209→- `agents/pm/prompt.ts` — `buildPmSystemPrompt()`: loads workspace projects and observations
   210→- `agents/pm/tools.ts` — `createPmTools()`: composes shared tools (search_entities, get_project_status, create_observation, suggest_work_items, create_work_item)
   211→
   212→**PM output schema:** `{ summary, suggestions: WorkItemSuggestion[], updated, discarded, observations_created }`
   213→
   214→The chat agent renders PM suggestions as `WorkItemSuggestionList` component blocks in the chat UI.
   215→
   216→### Observation Entity
   217→
   218→Observations (`observation/*`) are lightweight cross-cutting signals that agents write to the graph. They enable async agent-to-agent communication without forcing signals into wrong entity types.
   219→
   220→- **Severity levels:** `conflict` (contradictions needing human resolution), `warning` (risks), `info` (awareness)
   221→- **Lifecycle:** `open` → `acknowledged` → `resolved`
   222→- **Schema:** `observation` table with text, severity, status, category, source_agent, workspace, embedding
   223→- **Relation:** `observes` edge links observations to project/feature/task/decision/question
   224→- Agents load open observations as part of their context and factor them into their work.
   225→
   226→### Work Item Accept Flow
   227→
   228→When the PM agent suggests work items, the chat agent renders them as `WorkItemSuggestionList` components. Users can accept or dismiss each item:
   229→
   230→- Accept calls `POST /api/workspaces/:workspaceId/work-items/accept`
   231→- The endpoint creates a `task` or `feature` record in SurrealDB with embedding and optional project linking
   232→- Implemented in `entities/work-item-accept-route.ts`
   233→
   234→### Primary Chat Flow (`POST /api/chat/messages`)
   235→
   236→- `chat/chat-ingress.ts` validates/persists user input and registers an SSE stream message id.
   237→- `chat/chat-processor.ts` orchestrates async processing:
   238→  - load conversation + graph context
   239→  - run extraction (message and optional attachment chunks)
   240→  - persist entities/relationships/provenance
   241→  - transition onboarding state
   242→  - generate assistant response (onboarding reply or chat agent with subagent dispatch)
   243→  - emit SSE events (`token`, `extraction`, `onboarding_seed`, `onboarding_state`, `observation`, `assistant_message`, `done|error`)
   244→
   245→### RecordId and Table Access Rules
   246→
   247→- After request parsing, use `RecordId` objects everywhere for Surreal identifiers (never raw `table:id` strings in internal logic).
   248→- Server extraction types define typed record aliases:
   249→  - `GraphEntityRecord` and `SourceRecord` are `RecordId<UnionOfTables, string>` aliases.
   250→- Use `record.table.name` for table branching (the SDK's public API; `.tb` is an undeclared internal field that may break on upgrade).
   251→
   252→### RecordId Wire Format Contract (Strict)
   253→
   254→- Do NOT use one universal ID string format across all API fields. ID format is field-specific and enforced.
   255→- Fixed-table ID fields (for example: `session_id`, `task_id`, `project_id`, `workspace_id`) MUST be raw IDs only (UUID/string without `table:` prefix).
   256→- Polymorphic entity reference fields (for example: `entity_id`, `target`) MAY use `table:id`, but only when the field is explicitly documented as polymorphic.
   257→- Parse IDs exactly once at the HTTP/CLI boundary:
   258→  - fixed-table fields: `new RecordId("<known_table>", rawId)`
   259→  - polymorphic fields: parse `table:id` with table allowlist validation, then convert to `RecordId`
   260→- Never re-wrap prefixed values: reject fixed-table IDs containing `:` with a hard error instead of attempting recovery.
   261→- Never emit fixed-table IDs as `table:id` in API responses or CLI cache payloads. Emit raw IDs only.
   262→- If table context must be returned to clients, return it in a separate field (for example: `{ id: "<raw>", table: "task" }`), not by prefixing `id`.
   263→- `table:id` strings are for explicit polymorphic references only; they are not a general serialization format for all IDs.
   264→- Forbidden pattern: `new RecordId("agent_session", "agent_session:uuid")` (creates nested/mismatched IDs like `agent_session:⟨agent_session:uuid⟩`).
   265→- Any change touching ID read/write paths MUST include tests that cover:
   266→  - fixed-table round-trip (`raw -> RecordId -> raw`)
   267→  - polymorphic parse/validation (`table:id -> RecordId`)
   268→  - rejection of prefixed input in fixed-table fields.
   269→
   270→## SurrealDB KNN + WHERE Bug (v3.0)
   271→
   272→- SurrealDB v3.0 query planner silently returns empty results when a WHERE clause combines a KNN operator (`<|K, COSINE|>`, which uses the HNSW index) with a condition covered by a regular B-tree index (e.g. `workspace = $ws` when a `workspace` index exists).
   273→- Tables WITHOUT a B-tree index on the filtered field work fine with KNN + WHERE in the same clause.
   274→- Workaround: split into two steps — KNN in a `LET` subquery (HNSW index only), then filter by workspace in a second query (B-tree index only):
   275→  ```sql
   276→  -- BROKEN: both indexes conflict
   277→  SELECT ... FROM task WHERE workspace = $ws AND embedding <|20, COSINE|> $vec;
   278→
   279→  -- WORKS: separate index usage
   280→  LET $candidates = SELECT ..., workspace FROM task WHERE embedding <|20, COSINE|> $vec;
   281→  SELECT ... FROM $candidates WHERE workspace = $ws ORDER BY similarity DESC LIMIT $limit;
   282→  ```
   283→- Apply this pattern to ALL KNN queries on tables that have a regular index on the filtered field.
   284→
   285→## SurrealDB Full-Text Search (BM25)
   286→
   287→Reference: https://surrealdb.com/docs/surrealql/functions/database/search
   288→
   289→The UI entity search uses SurrealDB's built-in BM25 full-text search, not vector/KNN search. Vector search is reserved for the chat agent's `search_entities` tool where semantic similarity matters.
   290→
   291→### Setup
   292→
   293→Full-text search requires an analyzer and `FULLTEXT` indexes:
   294→```sql
   295→-- Analyzer with stemming (English snowball) and lowercase normalization
   296→DEFINE ANALYZER entity_search
   297→  TOKENIZERS blank, class, camel, punct
   298→  FILTERS snowball(english), lowercase;
   299→
   300→-- Per-field fulltext index (one index per field, not per table)
   301→DEFINE INDEX idx_task_fulltext ON task FIELDS title FULLTEXT ANALYZER entity_search BM25;
   302→```
   303→
   304→### Query syntax
   305→
   306→- Use the `@N@` match operator (N is a predicate reference number for `search::score`):
   307→  ```sql
   308→  SELECT id, title, search::score(1) AS score
   309→  FROM task
   310→  WHERE title @1@ $query
   311→  ORDER BY score DESC LIMIT 10;
   312→  ```
   313→- `search::score(N)` returns the BM25 relevance score for predicate N.
   314→- `search::highlight('<b>', '</b>', N)` returns text with matching tokens wrapped in tags.
   315→### Known limitations (SurrealDB v3.0)
   316→
   317→- `search::score()` and `@N@` do NOT work inside `DEFINE FUNCTION` — the predicate reference is lost across the function boundary. Search queries must run from the app layer. See: https://github.com/surrealdb/surrealdb/issues/7013
   318→- `@N@` does NOT work with SDK bound parameters (`$query`). The search term must be embedded as a string literal in the query. Escape single quotes before interpolation.
   319→- `BM25` without explicit parameters returns score=0. Always use `BM25(1.2, 0.75)`.
   320→
   321→### Entity search implementation
   322→
   323→Search queries run from the app layer (`entity-search-route.ts`) instead of SurrealDB stored functions due to the limitations above. Fulltext indexes are defined in `schema/migrations/0002_fulltext_search_indexes.surql`.
   324→
   325→## SurrealDB SDK v2
   326→
   327→Reference: https://surrealdb.com/learn/fundamentals/schemafull/define-fields
   328→
   329→- Do NOT use `.tb` on `RecordId` — it works at runtime but is not in the SDK type definition and may break on upgrade. Use `.table.name` instead (returns the same typed `Tb` string via the public API).
   330→- When using `http://` or `https://` URLs, the SDK uses HTTP transport only. It does NOT attempt WebSocket upgrade.
   331→- WebSocket is only used when the URL scheme is `ws://` or `wss://`.
   332→- To CREATE a record with a specific ID, use the SDK's `RecordId` class:
   333→  ```typescript
   334→  import { RecordId } from "surrealdb";
   335→  const record = new RecordId("table", "my-id");
   336→  await query("CREATE $record CONTENT $content;", { record, content: {...} });
   337→  ```
   338→- To SELECT a specific record by ID, use `RecordId` in the FROM clause:
   339→  ```typescript
   340→  const record = new RecordId("gladiator", id);
   341→  await query("SELECT * FROM $record;", { record });
   342→  ```
   343→- Do NOT use string-based record IDs like `table:id` in queries - use `RecordId` objects.
   344→- For optional record fields (e.g. `option<record<match>>`), omit the field instead of setting `null` - SurrealDB defaults to `NONE`.
   345→- Query results return `RecordId` objects for record references - cast directly, no string conversion needed.
   346→- Clause order: `SELECT ... FROM ... WHERE ... LIMIT ... FETCH ...` - `LIMIT` must come before `FETCH`.
   347→- **ORDER BY fields MUST be in the SELECT projection.** SurrealDB v3.0 raises a hard parse error (`Missing order idiom ... in statement selection`) when an ORDER BY field is not selected. This fails at query time, not at schema time, so it often hides until the query is actually executed. Always include every `ORDER BY` field in the `SELECT` projection. Example: `SELECT id, summary, created_at FROM decision ORDER BY created_at DESC` (not `SELECT id, summary ... ORDER BY created_at`).
   348→- Known issue: Surreal can throw `Expected a single result output when using the ONLY keyword` when a statement uses `ONLY` and returns no record output.
   349→- Workaround: force a return clause. In SDK calls that map to `ONLY` (for example `relate(...)`), use `.output("after")` so the statement returns a record.
   350→- Type query results directly. Access `RecordId.id` directly - do NOT create wrapper functions like `extractRecordId()`, `toString()`, etc:
   351→  ```typescript
   352→  const rows = await selectMany("SELECT id, name FROM gladiator WHERE totalWins > 0;") as Array<{ id: RecordId; name: string }>;
   353→  const result = rows.map((row) => ({ gladiatorId: row.id.id as string, name: row.name }));
   354→  ```
   355→- Do NOT use `FETCH` in queries if you need the raw RecordId reference. `FETCH` resolves references to full objects.
   356→- For `TYPE RELATION` tables, do NOT write edges with `CREATE`. `CREATE` produces non-relation records and will fail relation constraints. Use `RELATE` (or SDK `relate(...)`) to create actual relation edges.
   357→- For nested arrays (2D grids), use explicit type: `DEFINE FIELD grid ON match TYPE array<array<string>>;` - plain `array` silently rejects nested arrays in SCHEMAFULL mode.
   358→- Keep all Surreal tables in `schema/surreal-schema.surql` as `SCHEMAFULL`. Do NOT introduce `SCHEMALESS` tables.
   359→- In `SCHEMAFULL`, every persisted nested key must be explicitly declared. For `array<object>` fields, always define `field[*].subField` entries for all written properties.
   360→- Do NOT rely on permissive object inference for production payloads. If code writes a new key, update schema in the same change before deploy.
   361→- After schema changes, verify with `INFO FOR TABLE <table>;` in the target namespace/database to confirm nested fields are present.
   362→

   418→

   424→
   425→### Key SurrealQL graph syntax:
   426→```sql
   427→-- Create edge
   428→RELATE person:marcus->owns->project:brain;
   429→
   430→-- Traverse forward
   431→SELECT ->owns->project FROM person:marcus;
   432→
   433→-- Traverse backward
   434→SELECT <-owns<-person FROM project:brain;
   435→
   436→-- Multi-hop
   437→SELECT ->has_feature->feature->has_task->task FROM project:brain;
   438→
   439→-- Bidirectional
   440→SELECT <->conflicts_with<->decision FROM decision:d1;
   441→
   442→-- Edge with metadata
   443→RELATE decision:d1->conflicts_with->decision:d2
   444→  SET severity = 'hard', description = 'Contradictory deadlines';
   445→
   446→-- Recursive traversal (org tree, dependency chains)
   447→record:root.{..}.{ id, ->depends_on->task.@ };
   448→
   449→-- TYPE RELATION enforces edge-only tables
   450→DEFINE TABLE owns TYPE RELATION IN person OUT project | feature | task;
   451→```

   454→
   455→- **Vector Search Reference Guide:** https://surrealdb.com/docs/surrealdb/reference-guide/vector-search

   460→- **Full-Text to Vector Search Migration Guide:** https://surrealdb.com/blog/moving-from-full-text-search-to-vector-search-in-surrealdb
   461→- **Hybrid Search (vector + full-text with RRF):** https://surrealdb.com/blog/hybrid-vector-text-search-in-the-terminal-with-surrealdb-and-ratatui
   462→- **Search Functions (search::score, search::rrf):** https://surrealdb.com/docs/surrealql/functions/database/search
   463→- **Vector Functions (distance, similarity):** https://surrealdb.com/docs/surrealql/functions/database/vector
   464→
   465→### Key SurrealQL vector syntax:
   466→```sql
   467→-- Define embedding field + HNSW index
   468→DEFINE FIELD embedding ON conversation TYPE array<float>;
   469→DEFINE INDEX idx_conv_embedding ON conversation FIELDS embedding
   470→  HNSW DIMENSION 1536 DIST COSINE;
   471→
   472→-- KNN search (top 5 nearest neighbors)
   473→SELECT *, vector::similarity::cosine(embedding, $query_vec) AS similarity
   474→FROM conversation
   475→WHERE embedding <|5, COSINE|> $query_vec
   476→ORDER BY similarity DESC;
   477→
   478→-- Hybrid search (vector + full-text via RRF)
   479→LET $vs = SELECT id FROM conversation WHERE embedding <|5, COSINE|> $query_vec;
   480→LET $ft = SELECT id, search::score(1) AS score FROM conversation WHERE text @1@ 'decision about auth';
   481→RETURN search::rrf([$vs, $ft], 5);
   482→```

   516→
   517→## Platform-Specific Patterns
   518→
   519→### Pattern: Extraction Pipeline Write
   520→After the LLM extracts entities from a message, write them to the graph in a single transaction:
   521→```sql
   522→BEGIN TRANSACTION;
   523→  -- Create entities
   524→  LET $task = CREATE task SET title = $title, status = 'open', owner = $owner;
   525→  LET $decision = CREATE decision SET summary = $summary, status = 'extracted', confidence = $conf;
   526→  
   527→  -- Create relationships
   528→  RELATE $decision->decided_in->$conversation;
   529→  RELATE $decision->belongs_to->$project;
   530→  RELATE $task->belongs_to->$feature;
   531→  RELATE $person->owns->$task;
   532→COMMIT TRANSACTION;
   533→```
   534→
   535→### Pattern: Cross-Project Conflict Detection
   536→Traverse the graph to find related entities across projects:
   537→```sql
   538→-- Find all decisions in projects that share dependencies
   539→SELECT 
   540→  id, summary, status,
   541→  <-belongs_to<-project AS projects,
   542→  ->conflicts_with->decision AS conflicts
   543→FROM decision
   544→WHERE status IN ['extracted', 'proposed', 'confirmed']
   545→  AND <-belongs_to<-project != $current_project;
   546→```
   547→
   548→### Pattern: Context Packet for MCP Server
   549→Build a token-budgeted context packet for coding agents:
   550→```sql
   551→-- Active decisions for a project
   552→SELECT summary, rationale, status, decided_at
   553→FROM decision
   554→WHERE <-belongs_to<-project = $project
   555→  AND status IN ['confirmed', 'proposed']
   556→ORDER BY decided_at DESC
   557→LIMIT 20;
   558→
   559→-- Dependency chain for current task
   560→SELECT 
   561→  id, title, status,
   562→  ->depends_on->task.{id, title, status} AS dependencies
   563→FROM task
   564→WHERE id = $current_task;
   565→```
   566→

Cast directly with `as`.\n- Type result payloads once and avoid repetitive per-field casting.\n- Do NOT use module-level mutable singletons (e.g. `let cache` at file scope) for caching or shared state. Module-level state is shared across the entire process — when multiple server instances run concurrently (e.g. smoke tests with `--concurrent`), they silently corrupt each other. Pass shared state via dependency injection or use per-instance caches scoped to the owning object."
